statement.p: If \vec F is a path-independent vector field, with \int_{(0,0)}^{(1,0)}\vec F \cdot d\vec r = 5.7 and \int_{(1,0)}^{(1,1)}\vec F \cdot d\vec r = 3.4 and \int_{(0,0)}^{(0,1)}\vec F \cdot d\vec r = 4.7, find \int_{(0,1)}^{(1,1)}\vec F \cdot d\vec r.

static.solution: \int_{(0,1)}^{(1,1)}\vec F \cdot d\vec r by integrating from (0,1) to (1,1) by traversing the other three sides of the square with vertices (0,0), (1,0), (1,1) and (0,1). Thus \int_{(0,1)}^{(1,1)}\vec F \cdot d\vec r = \int_{(0,0)}^{(1,0)}\vec F \cdot d\vec r + \int_{(1,0)}^{(1,1)}\vec F \cdot d\vec r + \int_{(0,1)}^{(0,0)}\vec F \cdot d\vec r, so that \int_{(0,1)}^{(1,1)}\vec F \cdot d\vec r = \int_{(0,0)}^{(1,0)}\vec F \cdot d\vec r + \int_{(1,0)}^{(1,1)}\vec F \cdot d\vec r - \int_{(0,0)}^{(0,1)}\vec F \cdot d\vec r = 5.7 + 3.4 - 4.7 = 4.4.
